append.text: **Ps 79:2 *Qui regis Israël, inténde* → *Vós que regeis Israel, atendei*** — the row applied as foreseen (ὁ ποιμαίνων; the shepherd image stays in the next colon's sheep); passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked. *governais* (MS1932), *apascentais* options.

**Ps 79:4 = 79:8 = 79:20 *convérte nos* (God turning us; ἐπίστρεψον ἡμᾶς) → *convertei-nos*** — D25's exception as extended at 18:8 and 22:2 (God the agent, men the object); DRB, MS1932. The ambiguity reader heard personal/moral conversion first, restoration second — both the Latin's. Cost: 79:15 *convértere* (God turning himself) stays *Voltai-vos*, so the refrain and 79:15 no longer share a verb. *fazei-nos voltar* is option 2 (keeps the echo). **84:5 *Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster* (Compline) and 125:1 should follow this.** Passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 79:15 *Deus virtútum, convértere* → *Deus dos poderes, voltai-vos*** — the formula applied; passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 79:10 *Dux itíneris fuísti in conspéctu ejus* → *diante dela*** — a local departure (draft 1 had *à vista dela*): the stylist heard *à vista* first as 'in cash' and bureaucratic, the ambiguity reader lost the link of *dela* to the vine; the Greek is ἔμπροσθεν. **Evidence against *à vista de* with a third-person pronoun**; *à vista* remains an option there. Passed the Latinist.

**Ps 79:7 *Posuísti nos in contradictiónem vicínis nostris* → *Fizestes de nós contenda para os nossos vizinhos*** — the row, in 43:14's build without the article (stylist: *uma contenda* = one quarrel handed over). The ambiguity reader listed *contenda* unknown again and heard 'a reason for fighting' vaguely. *objeto de disputa* (MS1932) option. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 79:16 = 79:18 *quem confirmásti tibi* → *que firmastes para vós*** — a person as object (ἐκραταίωσας σεαυτῷ), the row's *firmar*; passed the Latinist twice. *fortalecestes* option; MS1932 *escolheste* interprets.

**Ps 79:14 *singuláris ferus depástus est eam* → *e pastou-a a fera solitária*** (κατενεμήσατο) — D43 applied; the ambiguity reader heard 'ate it' first, 'shepherded' possible (as 48:15). *devorou-a* (MS1932, DRB) option.
**Ps 79:16 *Et pérfice eam* → *E aperfeiçoai aquela que*** — the imperative the row had tried; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.
**Ps 79:3 *Éxcita poténtiam tuam* → *Despertai a vossa potência*** — the row; *virtútum → poderes* stands two verses on. No reader remarked.

**Ps 79:19 *vivificábis nos* → *vós nos vivificareis*** (after *E de vós não nos afastamos*, reordered so that *vós, vós* do not touch — stylist). Unknown to the ambiguity reader again; *vós nos dareis a vida* option.

**Ps 79:18 *Fiat manus tua super virum déxteræ tuæ* → *Seja a vossa mão sobre o homem da vossa direita*** — as 118:173; the stylist called *Seja … sobre* a calque and asked *Esteja* (a state; held, option).
**Ps 79:17 *ab increpatióne vultus tui* → *à repreensão do vosso rosto*** (vultus → rosto); the ambiguity reader heard 'at your angry rebuke'. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 79:5, 79:8, 79:15, 79:20 *(Dómine,) Deus virtútum* → *(Senhor,) Deus dos poderes*** (as 58:6); the refrain's growing titles kept (*Deus* → *Deus dos poderes* → *Senhor, Deus dos poderes*). The ambiguity reader heard 'God of all powers, abstract'. One decision (`virtutum`) with *dos exércitos* as option.
**Ps 79:13 *Ut quid destruxísti macériam ejus* → *Por que destruístes a sua cerca*** — *macéria → cerca* (φραγμός, as 61:4); no reader remarked.
**Ps 79:9 *Víneam de Ægýpto transtulísti* → *Transportastes do Egito uma vinha*** (μετῆρας) — the stylist asked *Trasladastes* (refused: D43); passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 79:5 *quoúsque irascéris super oratiónem* → *até quando estareis irado contra a oração*** — the future as copula + participle (the stylist: *vos irareis* is a knot of r's); *super* → *contra* as 73:1. Passed the Latinist.

terms: | excitáre (a power) | despertar (*Despertai a vossa potência*) | open | Ps 79:3 (ἐξέγειρον, rouse from sleep); safe at the *vós* imperative (past *despertei*). 77:17 *in iram excitavérunt*, 77:65 *excitátus est tamquam dórmiens*, 216 (canticle) *Éxcita furórem* (grep) — 77:65's sleeper fits *despertar*; 77:17 'provoke to wrath' may not. *Suscitai* (DRB 'stir up') option. |

| manifestári (imperative *manifestáre*) | manifestar-se (*manifestai-vos*) | open | Ps 79:2b (ἐμφάνηθι); kept apart from *osténdere → mostrar* in the refrain two verses on; safe (past *manifestei*). MS1932 *manifesta-te*. No reader remarked. |

| arbústa · pálmites · propágines (the vine's growth) | arvoredo · sarmentos · rebentos | open | Ps 79:11–12. *arbústa* are the trees a vine is trained on (L&S; ἀναδενδράδες): draft 1 *ramos* (DRB) drew a Latinist minor (narrows it, blurs it with *pálmites*), *arvoredo* taken, with the gapped *cobriu* supplied (the ambiguity reader heard the verbless colon as apposition). *sarmentos*, *rebentos* (MS1932) were unknown to the ambiguity reader, kept: three Latin words, three concrete Portuguese ones (rule 5). *palmes* elsewhere? (grep before settling). |

| vindemiáre | vindimar (*todos os que passam pelo caminho a vindimam*) | open | Ps 79:13 (τρυγῶσιν); MS1932. Unknown to the ambiguity reader; *colhem as uvas* option. 128:7 has *vindémia*? (not checked). |

| extermináre | devastar where a thing is ravaged (79:14, ἐλυμήνατο); *exterminar* where peoples are destroyed (43:3, ἐξωλέθρευσεν) | open | Ps 79:14 *Exterminávit eam aper de silva* → *Devastou-a o javali da selva* (DRB 'laid it waste'; L&S: in church Latin, to destroy); split by D15's Greek test. *exterminou* option. Other places (grep) decide by their Greek. |

| singuláris ferus | a fera solitária | open | Ps 79:14 (μονιὸς ἄγριος, the beast that lives alone); DRB's calque 'singular' would be heard as 'remarkable'; MS1932 *a fera selvagem* drops the word. Heard rightly by the ambiguity reader. |
| ejícere | lançar fora (*lançastes fora as nações*) | open | Ps 79:9 (ἐξέβαλες); MS1932. Kept apart from *expéllere → expulsar* (43:3). Other places (grep) should check their object. |

| suffódere | escavar (*Queimada a fogo, e escavada*) | open | Ps 79:17 (ἀνεσκαμμένη, dug up; L&S dig under); *arrancada* (MS1932) interprets. The feminine singular follows the Greek (the vine) where the Latin *incénsa … suffóssa* could also be neuter plural (DRB 'things'); the Latinist passed it twice with that noted. |
| cibáre | alimentar (*Com pão de lágrimas nos alimentareis*) | open | Ps 79:6 (ψωμιεῖς); 80:17 *Et cibávit eos ex ádipe fruménti* and 147:14 should check it (grep). *sustentar* (MS1932) option. |

| *potum dare … in mensúra* | *dar de beber … por medida* | open | Ps 79:6 *et potum dabis nobis in lácrimis in mensúra?* → *e nos dareis de beber em lágrimas, por medida?* — *in lácrimis* kept as a phrase (the Latinist, v1; draft 1 made the tears the object); *por medida* leaves open 'rationed' or 'full measure' (ἐν μέτρῳ); MS1932 *com abundância* is the Hebrew's. The ambiguity reader heard 'limited'. |
formulas: | *Deus, convérte nos: et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus* (79:4; 79:8 *Deus virtútum*; 79:20 *Dómine, Deus virtútum* — the refrain, the title growing; cf. 84:5 *Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster*, the Compline versicle — grep) | *Deus, convertei-nos: * e mostrai a vossa face, e seremos salvos* (79:8 *Deus dos poderes, convertei-nos*; 79:20 *Senhor, Deus dos poderes, convertei-nos*) | open — Ps 79; identical three times except the title; no object supplied to *osténde* (MS1932, DRB at 79:4 add 'us'); the stylist's best line |
